seo.metaTitle: Instagram Hashtag Generator: A Set That Actually Works
seo.metaDescription: Get Instagram hashtags in a balanced mix of big, medium and small tags, inside the 30 limit. Free, no login, nothing uploaded.

intro: Instagram gives you thirty hashtags and almost everyone spends them badly. The usual approach is to grab the thirty biggest tags in a category, which puts your post into feeds where several hundred thousand others arrive the same hour. You are visible for seconds. This Instagram hashtag generator builds the thing that actually works instead: a small number of big tags for the brief spike, a solid group of medium ones where your post stays near the top for hours, and a set of small specific tags where far fewer people are looking but the ones who are chose that exact subject. It runs in your browser with no account and nothing uploaded.
howto: Describe your post in plain words, the way you would say it out loud. The tool reads those words rather than needing keywords.
Check the topic it picked and correct it in one tap if it guessed wrong.
Set how many you want. The slider stops at Instagram's limit of thirty, but most accounts do better between eight and fifteen.
Press Build. Tap any hashtag you do not want and it drops out of the copy.
Copy the whole set, or copy just one group if you want to keep a block of medium tags and swap the small ones each post.
benefits: Instagram is the platform where the mix matters most, because it is the only one where thirty tags is normal and therefore the only one where people routinely waste all thirty on the wrong thing. A tag with two hundred million posts behind it is not an opportunity, it is a queue. A tag with forty thousand is a room you can actually be seen in. The three groups here are labelled with what they do rather than with a difficulty score, so after reading it once you can build sets yourself.

The small group is built partly from your own words, which is what stops every post in a niche carrying an identical block. Instagram notices identical blocks repeated post after post, and more importantly so does your audience, who stop seeing you in anything new. Try a different set reshuffles without touching your settings, so looking at three or four options takes seconds.
useCases: New and small accounts benefit most, because the broad-only approach hurts them hardest and the balanced mix is exactly what they are missing. Anyone posting several times a week uses it to vary the set rather than pasting the same saved block, which stops working faster than people expect.

Businesses posting product shots use it to reach past their existing followers into subject tags where buyers are actually browsing. Before you publish, our [hashtag counter](/tools/hashtag-counter/) checks the caption against the thirty limit and catches repeats, and the [caption formatter](/tools/caption-formatter/) keeps your line breaks from collapsing. If you post to several platforms, the [general hashtag generator](/tools/hashtag-generator/) covers all of them in one place.

faqs.q: How many hashtags should I use on Instagram?
faqs.a: Between eight and fifteen chosen carefully outperforms thirty broad ones for most accounts. The limit is thirty and going over does not fail the post; the extra tags are simply ignored. Quantity has never been the variable that matters.

faqs.q: Should hashtags go in the caption or the first comment?
faqs.a: It makes no measurable difference to reach, despite years of advice claiming otherwise. Putting them in the first comment keeps the caption clean in the feed, which is a presentation choice worth making for its own sake.

Instagram does restrict some tags, usually ones overrun with policy-breaking content, and a post carrying one can be hidden from that tag's page. The lists circulating online are mostly out of date. The practical protection is to use specific tags relevant to your subject rather than generic ones like #beauty or #followforfollow.

faqs.q: Why does the same hashtag set stop working?
faqs.a: Because it narrows you to the same audience every time and reads as automated. Keep your medium tags stable if they work, and change the small specific ones to match what each post is actually about.

faqs.q: Does this show how many posts each hashtag has?
faqs.a: No, and nothing free does honestly any more. Instagram stopped exposing those counts publicly, so anything claiming live numbers is scraping and breaks quietly. What this does instead is get the structure right, which is the part most people get wrong regardless.
No. The hashtag data and all the logic live in your browser. Nothing you type leaves your device and no account is needed.
